input:
The filling-line defect-reduction project was associated with a decrease in the reject rate from 5.4% to 3.4% during one quarter. Based on production of 354k units per year, this change corresponds to approximately 7080 fewer rejected units per year. It is important to note that the quarterly comparison is not adjusted for a planned shutdown that occurred during the same quarter. As a result, the two rates describe performance across a period that included production and shutdown-related interruption, rather than a cleanly isolated operating interval. The annual figure should therefore be interpreted as an annualised representation of the observed rate change at the stated production level, rather than as a separately counted total of avoided rejects. The available information does not separate the influence of the shutdown from the influence of the project, and it does not provide an adjusted reject rate for a shutdown-free comparison. Within those limits, the reported outcome is still a reduction between the starting and ending reject rates for the quarter, together with an annual avoided-unit estimate tied directly to the specified volume and dependent on the lower rate and operating pattern being sustained.

The shutdown also limits attribution, because the comparison period was not a uniform production interval and no separate rate is supplied for the time away from the shutdown. The result is best read as the change observed across the project quarter. Its annual form follows from applying that change to annual production, not from observing a full year at the lower rate.
target:
A defect-reduction project on a filling line cut the reject rate from 5.4% to 3.4% over one quarter. At 354k units per year, the change avoids about 7080 rejected units per year.

The annual figure applies the recorded rate change to the stated annual volume. It is an annual equivalent of the quarterly result, not a count accumulated over a full year, and it depends on the reduced rate applying at that volume under comparable conditions. The quarter included a planned shutdown; the rates are not adjusted for it. No shutdown-free rate is reported, and the project effect cannot be separated from any effect of the shutdown period in the figures given. The supported result is the recorded reduction over the quarter and the corresponding annual quantity of avoided rejects at the stated volume, with the shutdown left inside the measurement period rather than removed by adjustment.

The shutdown limits attribution. It formed part of the measurement period, and no separate rate is given for production outside it. The annual figure should therefore be used with its basis attached: a quarterly observed reduction extended to the stated annual volume. It should not be presented as an adjusted steady-state rate or as a count of rejects avoided over a completed year.
